label: PF Backlog 570
title: Delivery landing: gh pr merge --delete-branch fails when the head branch is checked out in a worker worktree -> false 'landing failed' after a successful merge
body: Observed delivering BI-PF-1254: the PR (gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch) MERGED on GitHub, but the command returned non-zero because gh then tried to delete the LOCAL branch, which is checked out by the worker/assignment worktree ('cannot delete branch ... used by worktree'). delivery._land treats non-zero as failure -> returns {'ok': False}, so deliver() BLOCKs the item and records no provenance even though the merge landed. Also '#31' hit a transient 'Base branch was modified. Review and try the merge again.' when develop advanced mid-run. RCCA: landing conflates 'merge this PR' with 'delete the local branch' (impossible when the branch is in a worktree); and has no retry for the transient base-modified race.

objective: Landing must reflect the PR's actual merge state: merge without trying to delete the worktree-held local branch (and/or tolerate that deletion failing), and retry once on the transient 'base branch was modified' error after re-updating the branch.
acceptance_criteria: gh pr merge runs without --delete-branch (or ignores local-branch-delete failure)
a merged PR yields ok=True + merge_sha even when the head branch is in a worker worktree
transient 'base branch was modified' retried once after gh pr update-branch
regression test: _land returns ok when gh merge succeeds but local-branch delete is impossible
approach: Remove --delete-branch from the gh merge call (GitHub already deletes the remote branch optionally; the local branch is owned by the worker worktree). On a non-zero result, if stderr mentions 'base branch was modified', re-run gh pr update-branch and retry the merge once; only then treat as failure.
verification: Objective achieved: Delivery landing: gh pr merge --delete-branch fails when the head branch is checked out in a worker worktree -> false 'landing failed' after a successful merge
risks: remote head branch may linger after merge (harmless; cleanup is separate)
must not mask a genuine merge failure (retry is bounded to 1 and only for the known transient)
